mainTopic: Vows against דגן and תבואה, and the story of רבא and רב יוסף about humility in תורה
overview: The משנה records a dispute about someone who makes a נדר against דגן. רבי מאיר says it also covers produce that is gathered into a pile, like the dry Egyptian bean. The חכמים say it covers only the five grains. The גמרא tests רבי מאיר's broad reading against a פסוק in דברי הימים, and אביי defends it. רבי יוחנן and a ברייתא teach that everyone agrees a נדר against תבואה covers only the five grains. When רב יוסף challenges this from the same פסוק, רבא answers that plain תבואה and תבואת שדה are different expressions. The גמרא then tells a story: רבא asks רב יוסף what the word עללתא includes, and רב יוסף becomes upset at how רבא treats his answer. רבא makes peace on ערב יום כיפור by mixing רב יוסף's wine himself. רב יוסף then asks him to explain a פסוק in במדבר, and רבא teaches that humility brings the תורה and greatness, while pride brings a person down. The proof that turning back from pride lifts a person up again continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute about a vow against דגן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with a disagreement. רבי מאיר says a נדר against דגן also forbids the dry Egyptian bean. The חכמים say it forbids only the five grains.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who vows off דגן may not eat the dry Egyptian bean. This is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say he is forbidden only in the five kinds of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents a נדר against דגן and two opinions about how far it reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about what the word דגן means. רבי מאיר reads it broadly, so it reaches a bean that is dried and gathered like grain. The חכמים read it narrowly: only wheat, barley, oats, spelt and rye.

keyTerms.meaning: The five grains: wheat, barley, oats, spelt, rye

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who vows off dagan (grain)
is forbidden to eat the dry Egyptian bean,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
he is forbidden only in the five species of grain.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a נדר against דגן includes the dry Egyptian bean. According to the חכמים, it includes only the five grains.

steps.title: רבי מאיר separates תבואה from דגן
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a נדר against תבואה covers only the five grains. A נדר against דגן covers everything gathered in a pile, but it does not include fruit from trees or vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: someone who vows off תבואה is forbidden only in the five grains. But someone who vows off דגן is forbidden in everything piled up, and he is still allowed fruit of the tree and vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר explains his position by contrasting two words for grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, תבואה is the narrow word and דגן is the broad word. Even his broad word has a limit: tree fruit and vegetables are not gathered into piles, so they stay permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain, produce (the narrower word for רבי מאיר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
One who vows off tevua (grain)
is forbidden only from the five species.
But one who vows off dagan
is forbidden in everything,
phrases.notes: He means everything that gets gathered into a pile, like the dry bean in the first line.

phrases.english: and is permitted fruits of the tree and vegetables.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַתְּבוּאָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי מאיר, a נדר against תבואה means only the five grains. A נדר against דגן means all piled produce, but not tree fruit or vegetables.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, דגן is the broad word and תבואה is the narrow word. The חכמים limit דגן to the five grains.

steps.title: Does דגן really mean anything that is piled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states what רבי מאיר seems to hold: דגן means anything gathered into a pile. It says this so it can test the idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is this to say that דגן means anything that gets piled up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the idea behind רבי מאיר's view. It is setting up a challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא links the word דגן to the verb for heaping up grain (מידגן). Once the idea is stated clearly, it can be checked against a פסוק.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Is this to say that 'dagan'
means anything that is piled up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the definition of דגן that רבי מאיר's ruling assumes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether דגן really means everything that is piled.

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges from a verse
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a פסוק that lists דגן and then also 'all the תבואה of the field.' If דגן already covers everything piled, the extra item seems hard to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: 'As soon as the matter spread, the people of Israel brought in abundance the first of grain, wine, oil… and all the produce of the field.' If דגן means anything piled, what is meant by 'as soon as the matter spread, they brought in abundance'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the broad definition of דגן using a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names דגן and then separately names 'all the תבואה of the field.' If דגן is already so broad, the second item seems to add nothing. רב יוסף asks what the abundance in the פסוק includes.

keyTerms.meaning: As soon as the matter spread

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
'And as soon as the matter spread,'
the children of Israel brought in abundance
the first of grain, wine and oil
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, added so the line matches the פסוק.

phrases.english: and all the produce of the field in abundance, etc.'
And if you say that dagan
means anything that is piled,
what is 'as soon as the matter spread, they brought in abundance'?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that דגן means anything piled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If דגן covers everything piled, the פסוק's extra 'all the תבואה of the field' seems to add nothing.

steps.title: אביי: the extra words add fruit and vegetables
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the extra phrase in the פסוק adds tree fruit and vegetables, which are not included in דגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the phrase comes to include tree fruit and vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the broad meaning of דגן by giving the extra phrase its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if דגן covers everything piled, it does not cover tree fruit or vegetables, because they are not piled. So 'all the תבואה of the field' teaches that the people also tithed those foods. This fits the משנה, where רבי מאיר permits tree fruit and vegetables.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It comes to include fruits of the tree and vegetables.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra words of the פסוק a separate meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If דגן already covers everything piled, the extra phrase would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra phrase adds tree fruit and vegetables, which are outside דגן.

steps.title: Everyone agrees about תבואה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the line in the משנה about תבואה. רבי יוחנן says that even the חכמים agree a נדר against תבואה covers only the five grains.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי מאיר says, one who vows off תבואה…' רבי יוחנן said: everyone agrees that one who vows off תבואה is forbidden only from the five grains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. רבי יוחנן says this point is not under dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the line is said in רבי מאיר's name, one might think the חכמים disagree with it. רבי יוחנן says they do not. The only dispute in the משנה is about דגן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
One who vows off tevua, etc.
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone agrees about one who vows off tevua
that he is forbidden only from the five species.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבי מאיר and the חכמים agree that a נדר against תבואה covers only the five grains.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: everyone agrees that a נדר against תבואה covers only the five grains.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: they agree that one who vows off תבואה is forbidden only from the five grains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'they agree' in the ברייתא shows that the חכמים do not argue with רבי מאיר about תבואה. This backs up רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
They agree about one who vows off tevua
that he is forbidden only from the five species.

steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's statement that everyone agrees about תבואה

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why anyone needed to teach this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for רבי יוחנן's statement and the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תבואה plainly means the five grains, there seems to be no reason to say that everyone agrees. The גמרא asks what this teaching adds.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the statement that everyone agrees about תבואה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems clear that תבואה means only the five grains, so there is no need to say it.

steps.title: Without it, we might think תבואה means everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought תבואה means every kind of produce. The teaching shows that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that תבואה means everything. So it teaches us that it does not mean everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which mistake the teaching prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תבואה can sound like 'all produce.' Someone could think it covers everything that grows. The teaching rules this out and limits תבואה to the five grains.

phrases.english: You might have said:
'tevua' means all things,
so it teaches us
that it does not mean all things.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a mistake the teaching prevents
steps.terutzMaskana: תבואה means only the five grains.

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges from the same verse
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings back the same פסוק. There, 'all the תבואה of the field' includes everything, so תבואה seems to mean all produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: 'And as soon as the matter spread, the children of Israel brought in abundance…'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף uses the same פסוק to challenge the narrow meaning of תבואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי already explained that the phrase in the פסוק includes tree fruit and vegetables. That suggests תבואה can mean everything, which goes against the teaching that it covers only the five grains.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
'And as soon as the matter spread, the children of Israel brought in abundance, etc.'
phrases.notes: The point is the end of the פסוק, 'all the תבואה of the field,' which covers every kind of crop.

steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that תבואה means only the five grains
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the פסוק, 'תבואה of the field' includes all crops, so תבואה seems to be a broad word.

steps.title: רבא: תבואה and תבואת שדה are different
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that plain תבואה and the phrase תבואת שדה mean different things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'תבואה' is one thing, and 'תבואה of the field' is another.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב יוסף by separating the two phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain תבואה means only the five grains, so a נדר using that word stays narrow. The phrase 'תבואה of the field' in the פסוק is wider and covers all crops. The פסוק does not change what plain תבואה means.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate, a thing of its own

phrases.english: Rava said:
'Tevua' is one thing,
and 'tevua of the field' is another.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to show that תבואה means all crops.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain תבואה means the five grains. Only 'תבואה of the field' is broad.
steps.whatToRemember: Plain תבואה in a נדר means only the five grains, and everyone agrees. The wider phrase 'תבואת שדה' is a different expression.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat תבואה and תבואת שדה as the same word. רבא's whole answer depends on keeping them apart.

steps.title: רבא asks what the word עללתא includes
steps.stepSummary: בר מר שמואל ordered that 13,000 זוזים be given to רבא from his עללתא. רבא asks רב יוסף what counts as עללתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The son of מר שמואל instructed that 13,000 זוזים be given to רבא from the crop of the Panya River. רבא sent a question to רב יוסף: what is called 'עללתא'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life case that depends on the meaning of a word. רבא needs to know what עללתא covers so he knows which money he can collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows straight from the last steps, which were about how far the word תבואה reaches. Now the same kind of question is asked about a different word, עללתא, in a case about money.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce, crop, or income from a property
What is it called? What does it include?

phrases.english: The son of Mar Shmuel instructed
that they should give thirteen thousand zuz to Rava
from the crop of the Panya River.
Rava sent it before Rav Yosef:
What is called 'alalta'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meaning of תבואה to the meaning of the similar word עללתא in a practical case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kinds of produce or income count as עללתא.

steps.title: רב יוסף answers from the ברייתא about grain
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers with the ברייתא: a נדר against תבואה covers only the five grains. So עללתא would cover only the five grains too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is taught already: they agree that one who vows from 'תבואה' is forbidden only in the five species.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers רבא by pointing to the ברייתא from step 7. He treats עללתא like תבואה, which means only the five grains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumes the two words have the same reach. If תבואה means only the five grains, then עללתא should mean only the five grains too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a taught source (here, the ברייתא quoted earlier)
The five grains: wheat, barley, spelt, oats, rye

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is a taught source:
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to the ברייתא from step 7.

phrases.english: And they agree about one who vows from 'tevua'
that he is forbidden only in the five species.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עללתא is like תבואה, so it covers only the five grains.

steps.title: אביי says the two words are not alike
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the comparison. תבואה means only grain, but עללתא means every kind of produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are they comparable? 'תבואה' means only the five species, but 'עללתא' means everything.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב יוסף's answer. He says you cannot learn עללתא from תבואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works only if the two words mean the same thing. אביי says they don't: תבואה is a narrow word, and עללתא is a broad word for all produce. So the ברייתא says nothing about עללתא.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Is it comparable?
'Tevua' means only the five species,
'Alalta' means all things.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא about תבואה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תבואה is a narrow word and עללתא is a broad word, so one cannot be learned from the other.

steps.title: רבא explains his real question: rent from houses and boats
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he already knew עללתא covers all produce. His real question is whether rent from houses and boats counts as עללתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought it back to רבא. He said: I never doubted that 'עללתא' means everything. My question is about rent from houses and boats. Since they wear down, maybe they are not 'עללתא'. Or since their wear is not noticeable, maybe they are.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא agrees with אביי that עללתא is broad. Then he states what he really wanted to ask: does rental income count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real crops come up fresh and do not use up the field. Houses and boats slowly wear down while you rent them out, so the rent might be partly using up the property itself. On the other hand, the wear is hard to notice, so maybe the rent still counts as a crop.

keyTerms.meaning: They lose value, they wear down
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with אביי. He agrees that עללתא means all produce. He is saying his question was about something narrower that nobody answered.

phrases.english: They brought it back before Rava.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: הָא לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי
phrases.english: He said: This was not a question for me,
that 'alalta' means all things.
This is what was a question for me:
Rent of houses and rent of boats, what is the rule?
Do we say: since they wear down,
it is not 'alalta'.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא יְדִיעַ פְּחָתַיְיהוּ —
phrases.english: Or perhaps: since their wearing down is not noticeable,
it is 'alalta'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts אביי's point and narrows the original question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether rent from houses and boats, which slowly wear down, counts as עללתא.

steps.title: רב יוסף is upset at being asked
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן report רבא's words to רב יוסף. He asks why רבא sent the question if he did not need help, and he becomes upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן told it before רב יוסף. He said: Since he doesn't need us, why did he send to us? רב יוסף became angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The story turns from the legal question to a personal one. רב יוסף feels that רבא brushed off his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף hears that רבא already knew what עללתא means. That makes the question look unneeded, and he takes offense. This sets up the next part of the story.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said it before Rav Yosef,
phrases.notes: They are reporting what רבא said in the last step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּלָא צְרִיךְ לַן,
phrases.english: He said: Since he does not need us,
why did he send to us?
Rav Yosef became upset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports רב יוסף's reaction to רבא's reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף was offended that רבא sent a question he seemed not to need answered.

steps.title: רבא comes on ערב יום כיפור and mixes רב יוסף's wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא hears about it and goes to רב יוסף on ערב יום כיפור. He takes over mixing the wine, and רב יוסף recognizes רבא's style of mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא heard and came before him on ערב יום כיפור. He found his attendant mixing a cup of wine for him. רבא said: Give it to me and I will mix it for him. The attendant gave it, and רבא mixed the wine. When רב יוסף drank, he said: This mixing is like the mixing of רבא בריה דרב יוסף בר חמא. רבא said: It is he.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא comes to make peace before יום כיפור by serving רב יוסף himself. רב יוסף recognizes the way the wine was mixed and realizes it is רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of arguing, רבא shows respect by doing the job of a servant. Then he openly says that he is the one who came.

phrases.english: Rava heard,
and came before him on the eve of Yom Kippur.
He found his attendant

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה קָא מָזֵיג קַמֵּיהּ כָּסָא דְחַמְרָא.
phrases.english: who was mixing a cup of wine before him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַב לִי דְּאֶמְזִיג לֵיהּ אֲנָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: Give it to me so that I will mix it for him.

phrases.aramaic: יְהַב לֵיהּ, וְקָא מָזֵיג אִיהוּ כָּסָא דְחַמְרָא.
phrases.english: He gave it to him, and he mixed the cup of wine.
While he was drinking, he said:
phrases.notes: The one drinking is רב יוסף.

phrases.english: This mixing is like the mixing

phrases.aramaic: דְּרָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא.
phrases.english: of Rava, son of Rav Yosef bar Chama.
He said to him: It is he.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע רָבָא, וַאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ בְּמַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְכִפּוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא responds to רב יוסף being upset by coming to make peace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא makes peace by serving רב יוסף, and רב יוסף recognizes him.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks רבא to explain a verse
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells רבא not to sit down until he explains the פסוק about מדבר, מתנה, נחליאל and במות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do not sit down on your feet until you tell me the explanation of this matter: What is meant by what is written: 'And from the מדבר, מתנה, and from מתנה, נחליאל, and from נחליאל, במות'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף accepts רבא and right away asks him a Torah question. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quarrel ends with Torah learning. רב יוסף asks what these place names in the פסוק are teaching. רבא answers in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't sit down (literally, on your feet or legs)
What is meant by what is written

phrases.english: He said to him: Do not sit down on your feet

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּאָמְרַתְּ לִי פֵּירוּשָׁא דְּהָדֵין מִילְּתָא:
phrases.english: until you tell me the explanation of this matter:
What is meant by what is written:
'And from the wilderness Mattana, and from Mattana Nahaliel,'
'and from Nahaliel Bamot'?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּיתֵּיב אַכַּרְעָךְ עַד דְּאָמְרַתְּ לִי פֵּירוּשָׁא דְּהָדֵין מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After making peace, רב יוסף asks רבא a question about a פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the list of place names in the פסוק means.

steps.title: The humble person rises: wilderness, gift, inheritance, heights
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that each place name in the פסוק shows a stage of growing through humility. A person who is open like a מדבר gets the תורה as a מתנה. Then God gives it to him as a נחלה, and he rises to במות, which means greatness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: When a person makes himself like a wilderness that is open to everyone, the תורה is given to him as a gift, as it says, 'And from the מדבר, מתנה.' Once it is given to him as a gift, God gives it to him as an inheritance, as it says, 'And from מתנה, נחליאל.' Once God gives it to him as an inheritance, he rises to greatness, as it says, 'And from נחליאל, במות.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב יוסף's request from the step before. He explains the place names in the פסוק as stages in a person's rise through humility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק lists stops on the journey through the desert. רבא reads each name by its meaning: מדבר is being humble and open to all, מתנה is a gift, נחליאל sounds like נחלו אל ('God gave it to him as an inheritance'), and במות means high places. Each stage leads into the next, so humility is the starting point for everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: like a wilderness: humble and open to everyone
a gift (also the name of a place in the פסוק)
God gave it to him as an inheritance (a wordplay on נַחֲלִיאֵל)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying anything about the real places on the map. He is reading the meanings of their names as a lesson about how a person gains the תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the answer to רב יוסף's test from the step before, and it shows רבא's skill. It also teaches the well-known idea that the תורה stays with someone who makes himself humble.

phrases.english: He said to him: Once a person makes
himself like a wilderness,
which is open to everyone,
phrases.notes: A wilderness belongs to no one, and anyone can walk through it. Such a person lets everyone step on him, with no pride.

phrases.english: the Torah is given to him as a gift,
as it says: "And from the wilderness, Mattanah."
And once it is given to him as a gift,
God gives it to him as an inheritance,
phrases.notes: He splits the name נחליאל into two words: נחלו (gave him as an inheritance) and אל (God).

phrases.english: as it says: "And from Mattanah, Nahaliel."
And once God gives it to him as an inheritance,
he rises to greatness,
as it says: "And from Nahaliel, Bamot."
phrases.notes: במות means high places, so here it stands for rising up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה כיון שעושה אדם את עצמו כמדבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's demand in step 18 to explain the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the place names מדבר, מתנה, נחליאל and במות in the פסוק mean.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They describe stages: humility leads to receiving the תורה as a gift, then as a lasting inheritance from God, and then to greatness.

steps.title: If he becomes proud, he is brought down into the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues with the next words of the פסוק. If the person who rose becomes proud, הקדוש ברוך הוא lowers him to the valley, and even sinks him into the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he raises himself up in pride, הקדוש ברוך הוא brings him down, as it says, 'And from במות, the valley.' Not only that, but he is sunk into the ground, as it says, 'And it looks out over the wasteland.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps reading the same פסוק. Now he shows the warning side: pride brings a person down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The journey in the פסוק goes from במות (heights) down to הגיא (the valley), so רבא reads this as a fall caused by pride. He then adds a second, deeper drop from the word ונשקפה. The ground-sinking image comes from the sound of the word, as the note on that line explains. Greatness from the תורה can be lost if a person becomes proud of it.

keyTerms.meaning: and not only that, but even more

phrases.english: And if he raises himself up,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings him down,
as it says: "And from Bamot, the valley,"
and not only that, but
he is sunk into the ground,
as it says: "And it looks out over the face of the wasteland."
phrases.notes: נשקפה sounds like אסקופה, a doorstep that is set down into the ground. That is how he gets 'sunk into the ground.'

steps.triggerLanguage: ואם הגביה עצמו הקדוש ברוך הוא משפילו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's reading of the same פסוק, moving from the rise to the fall.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words הגיא and ונשקפה על פני הישימון teach that pride brings a person low, even down into the ground.

steps.title: If he takes back his pride, God lifts him up again
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a hopeful ending. If the proud person regrets his pride, הקדוש ברוך הוא raises him up again. The proof from a פסוק comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he takes back his pride, הקדוש ברוך הוא lifts him up again...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins the last stage of his explanation: a fall is not final. The sentence continues past this section, where he brings his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the steps up and the steps down, רבא shows that the way back up is still open. חוזר בו means he turns back from his pride and becomes humble again. Then הקדוש ברוך הוא raises him once more.

keyTerms.meaning: takes it back, changes his ways

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's full picture: humility brings the תורה and greatness, pride brings a fall, and turning back from pride brings a person up again.

phrases.english: And if he takes it back,
phrases.notes: He means: if he turns away from his pride and becomes humble again.

phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, lifts him up

steps.triggerLanguage: ואם חוזר בו הקדוש ברוך הוא מגביהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the cycle that began in step 20: after the fall comes the chance to rise again.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person who regrets his pride is raised up again by הקדוש ברוך הוא. The proof from a פסוק follows.
